issues.description: Full compiled script is read into memory and shipped through every compile RPC response with no size bound.
issues.detail: The backend slurps the entire script into script_content on every compile, regardless of whether the user clicks Download. This duplicates bytes already addressable via the returned path, breaks the prior payload-size invariant, and wastes memory and bandwidth for large pipelines. Lazy-fetch on click via a separate endpoint, or read from the existing path on the client.

issues.description: File is opened without an explicit encoding, making decoding locale-dependent.
issues.detail: open(script_path) relies on the platform default encoding. Compiled Python may contain non-ASCII identifiers or docstrings; on a non-UTF-8 locale this raises UnicodeDecodeError or silently mangles bytes, failing a compile RPC that otherwise succeeded. Specify encoding='utf-8' explicitly at the read site, or drop the read entirely.

issues.description: compiledContent duplicates compiledPath as a place-oriented snapshot held in React state with no time semantics.
issues.detail: State now holds both the path identity and a string copy of that file's contents at one moment, passed down as a prop and never freed until the panel unmounts. Nothing ties the snapshot to a time; if the file is recompiled, the held string may silently disagree with the path. Fetch on click instead of snapshotting.

issues.description: Download icon is a clickable element but not a button; lacks keyboard accessibility and semantic role.
issues.detail: GetAppIcon with onClick is not focusable, keyboard-activatable, or exposed to assistive tech with a proper role. The adjacent Done indicator is correctly an anchor. Use an IconButton (or wrap in a button) with an aria-label so keyboard and screen-reader users can trigger the download. titleAccess alone is not enough.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the feature works but the shape is wrong: the entire compiled script is read on the server with no explicit encoding and shipped through every compile RPC response, then held as a duplicate snapshot in React state next to a path that already identifies the same bytes. This complects compilation with file-serving, breaks the prior payload-size invariant, and creates a locale-dependent decode failure mode that can break otherwise-successful compiles. On the frontend, the download trigger is an icon with onClick rather than a proper button, so it is not keyboard or screen-reader accessible. Recommended fix: split into a separate download/read endpoint (or read from the existing path) fired on click, specify utf-8 explicitly, and use a real IconButton with aria-label.
